We recommend using our Gradle plugin as it can add integrations and provide source context for events.

If you are manually adding multiple Sentry dependencies, you can add a [bill of materials](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/configuration/bill-of-materials.md) to avoid specifying the version of each dependency.

When running your application, please add our `sentry-opentelemetry-agent` to the `java` command.

Download the latest version of the `sentry-opentelemetry-agent-8.62.0.jar` from [MavenCentral](https://search.maven.org/artifact/io.sentry/sentry-opentelemetry-agent):

```bash
curl https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/sentry/sentry-opentelemetry-agent/8.62.0/sentry-opentelemetry-agent-8.62.0.jar -o sentry-opentelemetry-agent-8.62.0.jar
```

Then run your application with:

```bash
SENTRY_AUTO_INIT=false JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-javaagent:sentry-opentelemetry-agent-8.62.0.jar" java -jar your-application.jar
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: Java CLI argument*

## [Configure](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring-boot.md#configure)

Sentry's Spring Boot integration auto-configures `sentry.in-app-packages` property with the package where `@SpringBootApplication` or `@SpringBootConfiguration` annotated class is located.

Provide a `sentry.dsn` property using either `application.properties` or `application.yml`:

```properties
sentry.dsn=https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>

# Use Data Collection defaults but don't collect automatic user information.
# https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring-boot/data-management/data-collected/
sentry.data-collection.user-info=false
# Configure other data categories here.
# ___PRODUCT_OPTION_START___ performance

# Set traces_sample_rate to 1.0 to capture 100%
# of transactions for tracing.
# We recommend adjusting this value in production.
sentry.traces-sample-rate=1.0
# ___PRODUCT_OPTION_END___ performance
// ___PRODUCT_OPTION_START___ profiling

# Enable profiling
sentry.profile-session-sample-rate=1.0
sentry.profile-lifecycle=TRACE
// ___PRODUCT_OPTION_END___ profiling
// ___PRODUCT_OPTION_START___ logs

# Enable logs
sentry.logs.enabled=true
// ___PRODUCT_OPTION_END___ logs
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: yaml*

By default, only unhandled exceptions are sent to Sentry. This behavior can be tuned through configuring the `sentry.exception-resolver-order` property. For example, setting it to `-2147483647` (the value of `org.springframework.core.Ordered#HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE`) ensures exceptions that have been handled by exception resolvers with higher order are sent to Sentry - including ones handled by `@ExceptionHandler` annotated methods.

```properties
sentry.exception-resolver-order=-2147483647
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: yaml*

We recommend using Sentry's Spring Boot integration with one of the [logging framework integrations](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring-boot/logging-frameworks.md) as they work together seamlessly. To use Sentry **without** Spring Boot, we recommend using the [Sentry Spring integration](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring.md).

Once this integration is configured you can *also* use Sentry’s static API, [as shown on the usage page](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring-boot/usage.md), to record breadcrumbs, set the current user, or manually send events, for example.

## [Verify](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring-boot.md#verify)

This snippet includes an intentional error, so you can test that everything is working as soon as you set it up.

```java
import io.sentry.Sentry;

try {
  throw new Exception("This is a test.");
} catch (Exception e) {
  Sentry.captureException(e);
}
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: Kotlin*

Learn more about manually capturing an error or message in our [Usage documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/java/guides/spring-boot/usage.md).

To view and resolve the recorded error, log into [sentry.io](https://sentry.io) and select your project. Clicking on the error's title will open a page where you can see detailed information and mark it as resolved.

# Angular

title: "Angular"

# Sentry for Angular

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#prerequisites)

You need:

* A Sentry [account](https://sentry.io/signup/) and [project](https://docs.sentry.io/product/projects.md)
* Your application up and running
* Angular version `17.0.0` or above

Are you using Angular 16 or older?

If you're using Angular 16 or older, install and [Set Up the SDK Manually](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular/manual-setup.md). The Sentry Angular SDK still works for Angular versions 14 and newer but the installation wizards requires at least Angular 17.

## [Install](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#install)

Run the Sentry wizard to automatically configure Sentry in your Angular application. It will then guide you through the setup process, asking you to enable additional (optional) Sentry features for your application beyond error monitoring.

```bash
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i angular
```

Want to learn more about these features?

* [**Issues**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues.md) (always enabled): Sentry's core error monitoring product that automatically reports errors, uncaught exceptions, and crashes. If you have something that looks like an exception, Sentry can capture it.
* [**Tracing**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/tracing.md): Track software performance while seeing the impact of errors across multiple systems. For example, distributed tracing allows you to follow a request from the frontend to the backend and back.
* [**Session Replay**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/session-replay.md): Get to the root cause of an issue faster by viewing a video-like reproduction of what users saw in your app before, during, and after the problem.
* [**Logs**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md): Centralize and analyze your application logs to correlate them with errors and performance issues. Search, filter, and visualize log data to understand what's happening in your applications.
* [**Application Metrics**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md) (always enabled): Track and analyze custom application metrics, such as response times and database query durations, to understand trends and patterns in your application's performance and behavior over time.
* [**User Feedback**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback.md): Collect feedback directly from users when they encounter errors, allowing them to describe what happened and provide context that helps you understand and resolve issues faster.

This guide assumes that you enable all features and allow the wizard to add an example component to your application. You can add or remove features at any time, but setting them up now will save you the effort of configuring them manually later.

Prefer to set things up yourself? Check out the [Manual Setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular/manual-setup.md) guide.

What does the installation wizard change inside your application?

* Adds a `Sentry.init()` call into your `main.ts` file
* Registers the Sentry `ErrorHandler` and `TraceService` in your `app.config.ts` file
* Creates `.sentryclirc` with an auth token to upload source maps (this file is automatically added to `.gitignore`)
* Walks you through enabling source maps upload when making a production build, locally as well as in CI
* Adds an example component to your application to help verify your Sentry setup

## [Avoid Ad Blockers With Tunneling (Optional)](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#avoid-ad-blockers-with-tunneling-optional)

You can prevent ad blockers from blocking Sentry events using tunneling. Use the `tunnel` option in `Sentry.init` to add an API endpoint in your application that forwards Sentry events to Sentry servers.

This will send all events to the `tunnel` endpoint. However, the events need to be parsed and redirected to Sentry, so you'll need to do additional configuration on the server. The endpoint must forward only the request body to Sentry and accept only your own DSN. You can find a detailed explanation on how to do this on our [Troubleshooting page](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular/troubleshooting.md#using-the-tunnel-option).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  tunnel: "/tunnel",
});
```

## [Control the Data You Send to Sentry (Optional)](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#control-the-data-you-send-to-sentry-optional)

By default, the SDK sends user identity data (IP address, ID, and similar) and other data like HTTP bodies and URL query parameters. This will give you rich debugging context.

The SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

To send less data, turn off the categories you don't need in the `dataCollection` option. For the full list of categories and their defaults, [see the `dataCollection` options](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular/configuration/options.md#dataCollection).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  dataCollection: {
    userInfo: false,
    // other categories
  },
});
```

## [Verify](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#verify)

If you haven't tested your Sentry configuration yet, let's do it now. You can confirm that the Sentry SDK is sending data to your Sentry project by using the example component created by the installation wizard:

1. Open the page you added the example component to in your browser.
2. Click the "Throw error" button. This triggers an error.

Sentry captures this error for you. Additionally, the button click starts a trace to measure the time it takes for the error to be thrown.

##### Tip

Don't forget to explore the example component's code in your project to understand what's happening after your button click.

### [Verify Additional Features](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#verify-additional-features)

**Logs** (enabled by default)

See structured log entries from your application. You can send logs from anywhere:

```typescript
Sentry.logger.info("User action", { userId: "123" });
Sentry.logger.warn("Slow response", { duration: 5000 });
Sentry.logger.error("Operation failed", { reason: "timeout" });
```

Learn more about [Logs configuration](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular/logs.md).

**Application Metrics** (enabled by default) NEW

Track and analyze custom application metrics to understand trends and patterns in your app's performance and behavior over time:

```typescript
Sentry.metrics.count("checkout.failed", 1);
Sentry.metrics.gauge("queue.depth", 42);
Sentry.metrics.distribution("api_latency", 187, {
  unit: "millisecond",
});
```

Learn more about [Application Metrics](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular/metrics.md).

### [View Captured Data in Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/angular.md#view-captured-data-in-sentry)

Now, head over to your project on [Sentry.io](https://sentry.io) to view the collected data (it takes a couple of moments for the data to appear).

##### Important

Errors triggered from within your browser's developer tools (like the browser console) are sandboxed, so they will not trigger Sentry's error monitoring.

Need help locating captured data in your Sentry project?

* Open the [**Issues**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/issues/) page and select an error from the issues list to view the full details and context of this error. For more details, see the [Issue Details documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-details.md).
* Open the [**Traces**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/traces/) page and select a trace to reveal more information about each span, its duration, and any errors. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-basics/getting-started-tutorial/generate-first-error.md#ui-walkthrough).
* Open the [**Replays**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/replays/) page and select an entry from the list to get a detailed view where you can replay the interaction and get more information to help you troubleshoot.
* Open the [**Logs**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/logs/) page and filter by service, environment, or search keywords to view log entries from your application. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md#overview).
* Open the [**Application Metrics**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/metrics) page to view and analyze your metrics. For more details, see this [interactive walkthrough](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md#overview).
* Open the [**User Feedback**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/feedback/) page and click on individual feedback to see more details all in one view. For more information, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback.md).

# Sentry for Astro

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#prerequisites)

You need:

* A Sentry [account](https://sentry.io/signup/) and [project](https://docs.sentry.io/product/projects.md)
* Your application up and running
* Astro `4.0.0` or above
* If you're using Astro's Netlify adapter (`@astrojs/netlify`), you need version `5.0.0` or above

##### What runtime do you use?

This SDK currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions. If you use Cloudflare Workers or Cloudflare Pages, refer to our [Astro on Cloudflare guide](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.md). Other non-Node runtimes, like Vercel's Edge runtime, are currently **not supported**.

## [Install](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#install)

### [Install the Sentry SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#install-the-sentry-sdk)

Install the Sentry integration using the `astro` CLI, then install the Profiling package using your preferred package manager:

```bash
npx astro add @sentry/astro
npm install @sentry/profiling-node
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: yarn, pnpm*

## [Configure](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#configure)

**Error Monitoring** starts working as soon as you call `Sentry.init()`. **Logs** and **Application Metrics** need no extra configuration, and you'll learn how to send them in steps [#3](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#send-logs) and [#4](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#send-application-metrics-). This guide also enables **Tracing**, **Profiling**, **Session Replay**, and **User Feedback**.

Want to learn more about these features?

* [**Issues**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues.md) (always enabled): Sentry's core error monitoring product that automatically reports errors, uncaught exceptions, and crashes. If you have something that looks like an exception, Sentry can capture it.
* [**Tracing**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/tracing.md): Track software performance while seeing the impact of errors across multiple systems. For example, distributed tracing allows you to follow a request from the frontend to the backend and back.
* [**Profiling**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/profiling.md): Gain deeper insight than traditional tracing without custom instrumentation, letting you discover slow-to-execute or resource-intensive functions in your app.
* [**Session Replay**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/session-replay.md): Get to the root cause of an issue faster by viewing a video-like reproduction of what users saw in your app before, during, and after the problem.
* [**Logs**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md): Centralize and analyze your application logs to correlate them with errors and performance issues. Search, filter, and visualize log data to understand what's happening in your applications.
* [**Application Metrics**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md) (always enabled): Track and analyze custom application metrics, such as response times and database query durations, to understand trends and patterns in your application's performance and behavior over time.
* [**User Feedback**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback.md): Collect feedback directly from users when they encounter errors, allowing them to describe what happened and provide context that helps you understand and resolve issues faster.

### [Initialize the SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#initialize-the-sdk)

To configure Sentry on your app's client-side and server-side, create a `sentry.client.config.(ts|js)` and `sentry.server.config.(ts|js)` file in the root of your project. Use the tabs in the code box below to view the client and server configuration snippets.

The snippets also turn on:

* Tracing: via [`tracesSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/options.md#tracesSampleRate)
* Profiling: via `nodeProfilingIntegration()` and [`profileSessionSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/options.md#profileSessionSampleRate)
* Session Replay: via `replayIntegration()`, sampled with [`replaysSessionSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/options.md#replaysSessionSampleRate) and [`replaysOnErrorSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/options.md#replaysOnErrorSampleRate)
* User Feedback: via [`feedbackIntegration()`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/user-feedback/configuration.md)

Don't need a feature? Remove its integration and options from the snippets.

```typescript
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/astro";

Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  integrations: [
    // enables automatic instrumentation
    Sentry.browserTracingIntegration(),
    // enables Session Replay
    Sentry.replayIntegration(),
    // enables User Feedback
    Sentry.feedbackIntegration({ colorScheme: "system" }),
  ],

  // Enables Tracing.
  // Set to 1.0 to capture 100% of spans for tracing.
  // We recommend reducing this value in production.
  tracesSampleRate: 1.0,

  // Capture replays for 10% of all sessions,
  // plus for 100% of sessions with an error
  // Requires Sentry.replayIntegration()
  replaysSessionSampleRate: 0.1,
  replaysOnErrorSampleRate: 1.0,
});
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: Server config*

### [Register the Sentry Integration](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#register-the-sentry-integration)

Add the Sentry integration to your `astro.config.mjs`:

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";
import sentry from "@sentry/astro";

export default defineConfig({
  integrations: [sentry()],
});
```

### [Add Readable Stack Traces With Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#add-readable-stack-traces-with-source-maps)

To upload source maps for clear error stack traces, add your Sentry auth token, organization, and project slugs in the `sentry` options inside `astro.config.mjs`:

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";
import sentry from "@sentry/astro";

export default defineConfig({
  integrations: [
    sentry({
      org: "<your-org-slug>",
      project: "<your-project-slug>",
      // store your auth token in an environment variable
      authToken: process.env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN,
    }),
  ],
});
```

To keep your auth token secure, set the `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable in your build environment:

```bash
SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=<your-sentry-auth-token>
```

Using environment variables in Vite configs

Vite doesn't automatically load `.env` files into `process.env` when evaluating the config file. If you store your auth token in a `.env` file and want to access it via `process.env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, use Vite's [`loadEnv`](https://vite.dev/guide/api-javascript#loadenv) helper.

Alternatively, use a `.env.sentry-build-plugin` file, which the Sentry plugin reads automatically.

```javascript
import { defineConfig, loadEnv } from "vite";

export default defineConfig(({ mode }) => {
  const env = loadEnv(mode, process.cwd(), "");

  return {
    plugins: [
      sentryVitePlugin({
        authToken: env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN,
        // ...
      }),
    ],
  };
});
```

### [Control the Data You Send to Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#control-the-data-you-send-to-sentry)

By default, the SDK sends user identity data (IP address, ID, and similar) and other data like HTTP bodies and URL query parameters. This will give you rich debugging context.

The SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

To send less data, turn off the categories you don't need in the `dataCollection` option. For the full list of categories and their defaults, [see the `dataCollection` options](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/options.md#dataCollection).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  dataCollection: {
    userInfo: false,
    // other categories
  },
});
```

## [Send Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#send-logs)

Use `Sentry.logger` to send logs at different levels, such as `info`, `warn`, or `error`. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/logs.md) for all available logging methods and the syntax for formatting messages.

```javascript
Sentry.logger.info("User example action completed");

Sentry.logger.warn("Slow operation detected", {
  operation: "data_fetch",
  duration: 3500,
});

Sentry.logger.error("Validation failed", {
  form_field: "email",
  reason: "Invalid email",
});
```

If you already use `console`, capture those calls as Sentry Logs with [`consoleLoggingIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/logs.md#console-integration). We also provide integrations for:

* [Consola](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/logs.md#console-integration)
* [Pino](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/integrations/pino.md)

## [Send Application Metrics NEW](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#send-application-metrics-)

Use `Sentry.metrics` to send counters, gauges, and distributions from your app to Sentry. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Metrics](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/metrics.md) for all available metric types and configuration options.

```javascript
Sentry.metrics.count("checkout.failed", 1);

Sentry.metrics.gauge("time_since_refresh", 4, { unit: "hour" });

Sentry.metrics.distribution("api_latency", 187, {
  unit: "millisecond",
  attributes: { endpoint: "/api/orders" },
});
```

On Node.js, [`nodeRuntimeMetricsIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/configuration/integrations/noderuntimemetrics.md) also collects runtime health metrics automatically.

## [Verify Your Setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#verify-your-setup)

Let's test your setup and confirm that Sentry is working correctly and sending data to your Sentry project.

Add this button to a page in your Astro app and click it to send a test error:

```astro
<button id="test-error" type="button">Test Sentry Error</button>

<script>
  document.getElementById("test-error")?.addEventListener("click", () => {
    throw new Error("Sentry Test Error");
  });
</script>
```

### [View Captured Data in Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#view-captured-data-in-sentry)

Now, head over to your project on [Sentry.io](https://sentry.io) to view the collected data (it takes a couple of moments for the data to appear).

Need help locating captured data in your Sentry project?

* Open the [**Issues**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/issues/) page and select an error from the issues list to view the full details and context of this error. For more details, see the [Issue Details documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-details.md).
* Open the [**Traces**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/traces/) page and select a trace to reveal more information about each span, its duration, and any errors. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-basics/getting-started-tutorial/generate-first-error.md#ui-walkthrough).
* Open the [**Profiles**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/profiling/) page to see your slowest functions and an aggregate flame graph of your most frequent code paths. If tracing is enabled, select a transaction to see the flame graph for that part of your app. For more information, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/profiling/profile-details.md).
* Open the [**Replays**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/replays/) page and select an entry from the list to get a detailed view where you can replay the interaction and get more information to help you troubleshoot.
* Open the [**Logs**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/logs/) page and filter by service, environment, or search keywords to view log entries from your application. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md#overview).
* Open the [**Application Metrics**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/metrics) page to view and analyze your metrics. For more details, see this [interactive walkthrough](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md#overview).
* Open the [**User Feedback**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/feedback/) page and click on individual feedback to see more details all in one view. For more information, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback.md).

## [Next Steps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/astro.md#next-steps)

title: "AWS Lambda"

url: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda/
---

# Sentry for AWS Lambda (JavaScript)

Looking for instructions on how to add Sentry without modifying your code? [Check out these docs instead](https://docs.sentry.io/integrations/cloud-monitoring/aws-lambda.md).

On this page you'll get an overview how to install, configure and use Sentry in your AWS Lambda functions. Once set up, our SDK will automatically report error and performance data from your Lambda Functions. Issues in Sentry will automatically include cloudwatch data, function details and execution time measurements.

## [Installation](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda.md#installation)

Depending on your preferences, you can install Sentry in your Lambda functions using the [Sentry AWS Lambda Layer](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda/install/layer.md) (recommended) or the [Sentry AWS NPM package](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda/install/npm.md).

### [Should I use the Lambda Layer or the NPM package?](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda.md#should-i-use-the-lambda-layer-or-the-npm-package)

We generally recommend using the Lambda layer as it doesn't require you to deploy any Sentry dependency alongside your function. With the layer, you can achieve the same level of customization as with the NPM package. There are two reasons why you still might want to use the NPM package instead:

1. You want to minimize lambda function size and tree-shake parts of the SDK code that you don't need. A related reason might be because you're transpiling your code and want to transpile your dependencies as well.
2. You already use NPM packages and deploy `node_modules` with your function and you don't want to add a (or another) Lambda layer to your functions.

## [Configuration](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda.md#configuration)

After installing the SDK, you might want to configure some parameters. Besides the [common SDK configuration](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda/configuration.md), you can also [configure Sentry's Lambda Function handler wrapper](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda/configuration/lambda-wrapper.md) to optimize function runtime overhead and timeout warnings.

## [Verify](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda.md#verify)

Once set up, verify that Sentry is reporting errors correctly by throwing a sample error in one of your functions:

**\[CommonJS] index.js**

```javascript
exports.handler = async (event, context) => {
  throw new Error("This is a test error");
};
```

**\[ESM] index.mjs**

```javascript
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/aws-serverless";

export const handler = Sentry.wrapHandler(async (event, context) => {
  throw new Error("This is a test error");
});
```

## [Next Steps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/aws-lambda.md#next-steps)

* Explore [practical guides](https://docs.sentry.io/get-started/guides.md) on what to monitor, log, track, and investigate after setup

# Bun

**URL:** https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md

---
title: "Bun"
description: "Learn how to manually set up Sentry in your Bun app and capture your first events."
url: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/
---

# Sentry for Bun

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#prerequisites)

You need:

* A Sentry [account](https://sentry.io/signup/) and [project](https://docs.sentry.io/product/projects.md)
* Your application up and running

## [Install](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#install)

### [Install the SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#install-the-sdk)

Use the Bun package manager to add the Sentry SDK to your application:

```bash
bun add @sentry/bun
```

## [Configure](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#configure)

**Error Monitoring** starts working as soon as you call `Sentry.init()`. **Logs** and **Application Metrics** need no extra configuration, and you'll learn how to send them in steps [#3](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#send-logs) and [#4](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#send-application-metrics-). This guide also enables **Tracing**.

Want to learn more about these features?

* [**Issues**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues.md) (always enabled): Sentry's core error monitoring product that automatically reports errors, uncaught exceptions, and crashes. If you have something that looks like an exception, Sentry can capture it.
* [**Tracing**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/tracing.md): Track software performance while seeing the impact of errors across multiple systems. For example, distributed tracing allows you to follow a request from the frontend to the backend and back.
* [**Logs**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md): Centralize and analyze your application logs to correlate them with errors and performance issues. Search, filter, and visualize log data to understand what's happening in your applications.
* [**Application Metrics**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md) (always enabled): Track and analyze custom application metrics, such as response times and database query durations, to understand trends and patterns in your application's performance and behavior over time.

### [Initialize the Sentry SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#initialize-the-sentry-sdk)

Sentry should be initialized as early in your app as possible. Create a file named `instrument.js` in the root directory of your project and add the code snippet shown below.

The snippet also turns on:

* Tracing: via [`tracesSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/configuration/options.md#tracesSampleRate)

Don't need a feature? Remove its integration and options from the snippet.

```javascript
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";

// Ensure to call this before importing any other modules!
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  // Enables Tracing.
  // Set to 1.0 to capture 100% of spans for tracing.
  // We recommend reducing this value in production.
  tracesSampleRate: 1.0,
});
```

### [Build With the Sentry Plugin (Recommended)](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#build-with-the-sentry-plugin-recommended)

We recommend building with the Sentry plugin, because it adds spans from your dependencies, such as database drivers, AI SDKs, and web frameworks like Express, Koa and Hapi. Bun has no runtime hook Sentry can use to instrument those packages, so the plugin rewrites them as `bun build` bundles them.

Add `sentryBunPlugin` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` to your `Bun.build()` call, then run the output the same way, with `--preload`. Errors, the spans you create yourself, and `Bun.serve`, `node:http` and `fetch` spans work either way.

```typescript
import { sentryBunPlugin } from "@sentry/bun/plugin";

await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./app.ts"],
  outdir: "./dist",
  target: "bun",
  plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()],
});
```

### [Apply Instrumentation to Your App](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#apply-instrumentation-to-your-app)

Preload your instrumentation file with the [`--preload`](https://bun.com/docs/runtime#param-preload) flag. This is what guarantees that `Sentry.init()` runs before any other module is loaded.

```bash
bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: Built output*

### [Add Readable Stack Traces With Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#add-readable-stack-traces-with-source-maps)

The stack traces in your Sentry errors probably won't look like your actual code without unminifying them. To fix this, upload your source maps to Sentry. The easiest way to do this is by using the Sentry Wizard.

Alternatively, take a look at our [Uploading Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/sourcemaps/uploading.md) documentation.

```bash
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i sourcemaps
```

### [Control the Data You Send to Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#control-the-data-you-send-to-sentry)

By default, the SDK sends user identity data (IP address, ID, and similar) and other data like HTTP bodies and URL query parameters. This will give you rich debugging context.

The SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

To send less data, turn off the categories you don't need in the `dataCollection` option. For the full list of categories and their defaults, [see the `dataCollection` options](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/configuration/options.md#dataCollection).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  dataCollection: {
    userInfo: false,
    // other categories
  },
});
```

## [Send Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#send-logs)

Use `Sentry.logger` to send logs at different levels, such as `info`, `warn`, or `error`. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/logs.md) for all available logging methods and the syntax for formatting messages.

```javascript
Sentry.logger.info("User example action completed");

Sentry.logger.warn("Slow operation detected", {
  operation: "data_fetch",
  duration: 3500,
});

Sentry.logger.error("Validation failed", {
  form_field: "email",
  reason: "Invalid email",
});
```

If you're already logging with another library, use an integration to capture those logs as Sentry Logs automatically:

* [`consoleLoggingIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/logs.md#console-integration) for `console` calls
* [Consola](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/logs.md#console-integration)
* [Pino](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/configuration/integrations/pino.md)

## [Send Application Metrics NEW](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#send-application-metrics-)

Use `Sentry.metrics` to send counters, gauges, and distributions from your app to Sentry. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Metrics](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/metrics.md) for all available metric types and configuration options.

```javascript
Sentry.metrics.count("checkout.failed", 1);

Sentry.metrics.gauge("time_since_refresh", 4, { unit: "hour" });

Sentry.metrics.distribution("api_latency", 187, {
  unit: "millisecond",
  attributes: { endpoint: "/api/orders" },
});
```

For Bun, [`bunRuntimeMetricsIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/configuration/integrations/bunruntimemetrics.md) also collects runtime health metrics automatically.

## [Verify Your Setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#verify-your-setup)

Let's test your setup and confirm that Sentry is working correctly and sending data to your Sentry project.

Add an intentional error to your main application file:

```javascript
setTimeout(() => {
  throw new Error("Sentry Test Error");
}, 0);
```

### [View Captured Data in Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#view-captured-data-in-sentry)

Finally, head over to your project on [Sentry.io](https://sentry.io/) to view the collected data (it takes a couple of moments for the data to appear).

Need help locating captured data in your Sentry project?

* Open the [**Issues**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/issues/) page and select an error from the issues list to view the full details and context of this error. For more details, see the [Issue Details documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-details.md).
* Open the [**Traces**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/traces/) page and select a trace to reveal more information about each span, its duration, and any errors. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-basics/getting-started-tutorial/generate-first-error.md#ui-walkthrough).
* Open the [**Logs**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/logs/) page and filter by service, environment, or search keywords to view log entries from your application. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md#overview).
* Open the [**Application Metrics**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/metrics) page to view and analyze your metrics. For more details, see this [interactive walkthrough](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md#overview).

## [Next Steps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun.md#next-steps)

At this point, you should have integrated Sentry into your Bun application. Here's what to explore next:

* Explore [practical guides](https://docs.sentry.io/get-started/guides.md) on what to monitor, log, track, and investigate after setup
* [Set up Agent Tracing](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/agent-tracing.md) to monitor your AI systems

Are you having problems setting up the SDK?

* Find various topics in [Troubleshooting](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/troubleshooting.md)
* [Get support](https://www.sentry.help/en/)

# Azure Functions

**URL:** https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md

---
title: "Azure Functions"
description: "Learn how to manually set up Sentry in your Azure Functions and capture your first events."
url: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/
---

# Sentry for Azure Functions (JavaScript)

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#prerequisites)

You need:

* A Sentry [account](https://sentry.io/signup/) and [project](https://docs.sentry.io/product/projects.md)
* Your application up and running
* Node version `20.19.0` or above. Node.js 22 needs `22.12` or higher, while Node.js 23 needs `23.2` or higher (`>=20.19.0 <22.0.0 || >=22.12.0 <23.0.0 || >=23.2.0`).

## [Install](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#install)

### [Install the Sentry SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#install-the-sentry-sdk)

Run the command for your preferred package manager to add `@sentry/node` as a runtime dependency to your application:

```bash
npm install @sentry/node --save
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: yarn, pnpm*

```bash
npm install @sentry/node @sentry/profiling-node --save
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: yarn, pnpm*

## [Configure](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#configure)

**Error Monitoring** starts working as soon as you call `Sentry.init()`. **Logs** and **Application Metrics** need no extra configuration, and you'll learn how to send them in steps [#3](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#send-logs) and [#4](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#send-application-metrics-). This guide also enables **Tracing** and **Profiling**.

Want to learn more about these features?

* [**Issues**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues.md) (always enabled): Sentry's core error monitoring product that automatically reports errors, uncaught exceptions, and crashes. If you have something that looks like an exception, Sentry can capture it.
* [**Tracing**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/tracing.md): Track software performance while seeing the impact of errors across multiple systems. For example, distributed tracing allows you to follow a request from the frontend to the backend and back.
* [**Profiling**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/profiling.md): Gain deeper insight than traditional tracing without custom instrumentation, letting you discover slow-to-execute or resource-intensive functions in your app.
* [**Logs**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md): Centralize and analyze your application logs to correlate them with errors and performance issues. Search, filter, and visualize log data to understand what's happening in your applications.
* [**Application Metrics**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md) (always enabled): Track and analyze custom application metrics, such as response times and database query durations, to understand trends and patterns in your application's performance and behavior over time.

The snippet also turns on:

* Tracing: via [`tracesSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/configuration/options.md#tracesSampleRate)
* Profiling: via [`profileSessionSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/configuration/options.md#profileSessionSampleRate) and [`nodeProfilingIntegration()`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/configuration/integrations/nodeprofiling.md)

Don't need a feature? Remove its integration and options from the snippet.

Make sure to initialize Sentry at the top of your function file before importing any other modules:

```javascript
const Sentry = require("@sentry/node");
const { nodeProfilingIntegration } = require("@sentry/profiling-node");
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",

  integrations: [nodeProfilingIntegration()],
  // Enables Tracing.
  // Set to 1.0 to capture 100% of spans for tracing.
  // We recommend reducing this value in production.
  tracesSampleRate: 1.0,

  // Enables Profiling.
  // Set to 1.0 to profile every session.
  // We recommend reducing this value in production.
  profileSessionSampleRate: 1.0,
});

// your function code
```

### [Capture Errors](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#capture-errors)

Because Azure Functions are short-lived, you have to explicitly `flush` Sentry events after calling `captureException`, or they may be lost before being sent to Sentry.

```javascript
const Sentry = require("@sentry/node");

// your Sentry init code

module.exports = async function (context, req) {
  try {
    // Your function code
  } catch (e) {
    // use Sentry.withScope to enrich the event with request data
    Sentry.withScope((scope) => {
      // Attach request context (requires dataCollection: { userInfo: true })
      scope.setSDKProcessingMetadata({ request: req });
      Sentry.captureException(e);
    });
    await Sentry.flush(2000);
  }
  // ...
};
```

### [Add Readable Stack Traces With Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#add-readable-stack-traces-with-source-maps)

The stack traces in your Sentry errors probably won't look like your actual code without unminifying them. To fix this, upload your source maps to Sentry. The easiest way to do this is by using the Sentry Wizard.

Alternatively, take a look at our [Uploading Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/sourcemaps/uploading.md) documentation.

```bash
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i sourcemaps
```

### [Control the Data You Send to Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#control-the-data-you-send-to-sentry)

By default, the SDK sends user identity data (IP address, ID, and similar) and other data like HTTP bodies and URL query parameters. This will give you rich debugging context.

The SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

To send less data, turn off the categories you don't need in the `dataCollection` option. For the full list of categories and their defaults, [see the `dataCollection` options](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/configuration/options.md#dataCollection).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  dataCollection: {
    userInfo: false,
    // other categories
  },
});
```

## [Send Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#send-logs)

Use `Sentry.logger` to send logs at different levels, such as `info`, `warn`, or `error`. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/logs.md) for all available logging methods and the syntax for formatting messages.

```javascript
Sentry.logger.info("User example action completed");

Sentry.logger.warn("Slow operation detected", {
  operation: "data_fetch",
  duration: 3500,
});

Sentry.logger.error("Validation failed", {
  form_field: "email",
  reason: "Invalid email",
});
```

If you're already logging with another library, use an integration to capture those logs as Sentry Logs automatically:

* [`consoleLoggingIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/logs.md#console-integration) for `console` calls
* [Consola](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/logs.md#console-integration)
* [Pino](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/configuration/integrations/pino.md)

## [Send Application Metrics NEW](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#send-application-metrics-)

Use `Sentry.metrics` to send counters, gauges, and distributions from your app to Sentry. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Metrics](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/metrics.md) for all available metric types and configuration options.

```javascript
Sentry.metrics.count("checkout.failed", 1);

Sentry.metrics.gauge("time_since_refresh", 4, { unit: "hour" });

Sentry.metrics.distribution("api_latency", 187, {
  unit: "millisecond",
  attributes: { endpoint: "/api/orders" },
});
```

On Node.js, [`nodeRuntimeMetricsIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions/configuration/integrations/noderuntimemetrics.md) also collects runtime health metrics automatically.

## [Verify Your Setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#verify-your-setup)

Let's test your setup and confirm that Sentry is working correctly and sending data to your Sentry project.

Add an intentional error in your function and flush the event before the function execution ends:

```javascript
const Sentry = require("@sentry/node");

module.exports = async function (context, req) {
  try {
    throw new Error("Sentry Test Error");
  } catch (error) {
    Sentry.captureException(error);
    await Sentry.flush(2000);
  }
};
```

### [View Captured Data in Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/azure-functions.md#view-captured-data-in-sentry)

Now, head over to your project on [Sentry.io](https://sentry.io/) to view the collected data (it takes a couple of moments for the data to appear).

Need help locating captured data in your Sentry project?

* Open the [**Issues**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/issues/) page and select an error from the issues list to view the full details and context of this error. For more details, see the [Issue Details documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-details.md).
* Open the [**Traces**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/traces/) page and select a trace to reveal more information about each span, its duration, and any errors. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-basics/getting-started-tutorial/generate-first-error.md#ui-walkthrough).
* Open the [**Profiles**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/profiling/) page to see your slowest functions and an aggregate flame graph of your most frequent code paths. If tracing is enabled, select a transaction to see the flame graph for that part of your app. For more information, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/profiling/profile-details.md).
* Open the [**Logs**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/logs/) page and filter by service, environment, or search keywords to view log entries from your application. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md#overview).
* Open the [**Application Metrics**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/metrics) page to view and analyze your metrics. For more details, see this [interactive walkthrough](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md#overview).

# Capacitor

**URL:** https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md

---
title: "Capacitor"
description: "Learn how to set up Sentry in your Capacitor application, capture your first events and traces, and view them in Sentry."
url: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/
---

# Sentry for Capacitor

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#prerequisites)

You need:

* A Sentry [account](https://sentry.io/signup/) and [project](https://docs.sentry.io/product/projects.md)
* Your application up and running

This guide will show you setup instructions for Angular, React, Vue, and Nuxt. If you use any other JavaScript framework (or none at all) with Capacitor, follow the vanilla instructions outlined under "Other".

## [Install](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#install)

### [Install the Sentry SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#install-the-sentry-sdk)

Run the command for your preferred package manager to add Sentry's Capacitor SDK and the SDK for the framework you're using to your application:

**Angular**

```bash
# npm
npm install @sentry/capacitor @sentry/angular --save

# yarn
yarn add @sentry/capacitor @sentry/angular

# pnpm
pnpm add @sentry/capacitor @sentry/angular
```

**React**

```bash
# npm
npm install @sentry/capacitor @sentry/react --save
```

Notes on framework compatibility

#### [Angular](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#angular)

Currently, the Sentry Capacitor SDK only supports Angular 14 and newer. If you're using an older version of Angular, you also need to use an older version of the SDK. See this table for compatibility guidance:

| Angular version | Recommended Sentry SDK                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 14 and newer    | `@sentry/capacitor` `@sentry/angular`             |
| 12 or 13        | `@sentry/capacitor^0` `@sentry/angular-ivy@^7` \* |
| 10 or 11        | `@sentry/capacitor^0` `@sentry/angular@^7` \*     |

\* These versions of the SDK are no longer maintained or tested. Version 0 might still receive bug fixes, but we don't guarantee support.

### [React and Vue](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#react-and-vue)

Both frameworks are fully compatible with the current and beta versions of Sentry Capacitor.

## [Configure](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#configure)

**Error Monitoring** starts working as soon as you call `Sentry.init()`. **Logs** need no extra configuration, and you'll learn how to send them in step [#3](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#send-logs). This guide also enables **Tracing**, **Session Replay**, and **User Feedback**.

Want to learn more about these features?

* [**Issues**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues.md) (always enabled): Sentry's core error monitoring product that automatically reports errors, uncaught exceptions, and crashes. If you have something that looks like an exception, Sentry can capture it.
* [**Tracing**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/tracing.md): Track software performance while seeing the impact of errors across multiple systems. For example, distributed tracing allows you to follow a request from the frontend to the backend and back.
* [**Session Replay**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/session-replay.md): Get to the root cause of an issue faster by viewing a video-like reproduction of what users saw in your app before, during, and after the problem.
* [**Logs**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md): Centralize and analyze your application logs to correlate them with errors and performance issues. Search, filter, and visualize log data to understand what's happening in your applications.
* [**User Feedback**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback.md): Collect feedback directly from users when they encounter errors, allowing them to describe what happened and provide context that helps you understand and resolve issues faster.

### [Initialize the Sentry SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#initialize-the-sentry-sdk)

Initialize Sentry as early as possible in your application's lifecycle.

The snippets also turn on:

* Tracing: via [`tracesSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/configuration/options.md#tracesSampleRate)
* Session Replay: via `replayIntegration()`, sampled with [`replaysSessionSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/configuration/options.md#replaysSessionSampleRate) and [`replaysOnErrorSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/configuration/options.md#replaysOnErrorSampleRate)
* User Feedback: via [`feedbackIntegration()`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/user-feedback/configuration.md)

Don't need a feature? Remove its integration and options from the snippet.

If you're using Angular, React, Vue, or Nuxt, make sure to forward the `init` method from the framework's Sentry SDK, as you can see in these code snippets. If you're following the vanilla setup, you don't need to do this.

**\[Angular 14+] app.module.ts**

```typescript
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/capacitor";
import * as SentryAngular from "@sentry/angular";

Sentry.init(
  {
    dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",

    // Set your release version, such as "getsentry@1.0.0"
    release: "my-project-name@<release-name>",
    // Set your dist version, such as "1"
    dist: "<dist>",
    integrations: [
      // Enables automatic instrumentation
      Sentry.browserTracingIntegration(),
      // enables Session Replay
      Sentry.replayIntegration(),
      // enables User Feedback
      Sentry.feedbackIntegration({
        // Additional integration configuration goes in here
        colorScheme: "system",
      }),
    ],

    // Enables Tracing.
    // Set to 1.0 to capture 100% of spans for tracing.
    // We recommend reducing this value in production.
    tracesSampleRate: 1.0,

    // Limit which URLs receive trace propagation
    tracePropagationTargets: ["localhost", /^https:\/\/yourserver\.io\/api/],

    // Capture replays for 10% of all sessions,
    // plus for 100% of sessions with an error
    // Requires Sentry.replayIntegration()
    replaysSessionSampleRate: 0.1,
    replaysOnErrorSampleRate: 1.0,
  },
  // Forward the init method from @sentry/angular
  SentryAngular.init
);

@NgModule({
  providers: [
    {
      provide: ErrorHandler,
      // Attach the Sentry ErrorHandler
      useValue: SentryAngular.createErrorHandler(),
    },
    {
      provide: SentryAngular.TraceService,
      deps: [Router],
    },
    {
      provide: APP_INITIALIZER,
      useFactory: () => () => {},
      deps: [SentryAngular.TraceService],
      multi: true,
    },
  ],
})
```

**\[Angular 12, 13] app.module.ts**

### [Add Readable Stack Traces With Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#add-readable-stack-traces-with-source-maps)

The stack traces in your Sentry errors probably won't look like your actual code without unminifying them. To fix this, upload your source maps to Sentry. The easiest way to do this is by using the Sentry Wizard.

Alternatively, take a look at our [Uploading Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/sourcemaps/uploading.md) documentation.

```bash
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i sourcemaps
```

### [Provide Native Debug Information for iOS](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#provide-native-debug-information-for-ios)

You need to provide debug information to Sentry to make the stack-trace information for native crashes on iOS easier to understand. You can provide debug information by [uploading dSYM files](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/dsym.md).

### [Control the Data You Send to Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#control-the-data-you-send-to-sentry)

By default, the SDK sends user identity data (IP address, ID, and similar) and other data like HTTP bodies and URL query parameters. This will give you rich debugging context.

The SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

To send less data, turn off the categories you don't need in the `dataCollection` option. For the full list of categories and their defaults, [see the `dataCollection` options](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/configuration/options.md#dataCollection).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  dataCollection: {
    userInfo: false,
    // other categories
  },
});
```

## [Send Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#send-logs)

Use `Sentry.logger` to send logs at different levels, such as `info`, `warn`, or `error`. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/logs.md) for all available logging methods and the syntax for formatting messages.

```javascript
Sentry.logger.info("User example action completed");

Sentry.logger.warn("Slow operation detected", {
  operation: "data_fetch",
  duration: 3500,
});

Sentry.logger.error("Validation failed", {
  form_field: "email",
  reason: "Invalid email",
});
```

If you already use `console`, capture those calls as Sentry Logs with [`consoleLoggingIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor/logs.md#console-integration).

## [Verify Your Setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#verify-your-setup)

Let's test your setup and confirm that Sentry is working correctly and sending data to your Sentry project.

Add a test button to an existing page. Clicking it throws an error that Sentry captures:

##### Important

Errors triggered from within your browser's developer tools (like the browser console) are sandboxed, so they will not trigger Sentry's error monitoring.

```html
<button type="button" id="test-sentry-error">Test Sentry Error</button>

<script type="module">
  document
    .getElementById("test-sentry-error")
    .addEventListener("click", () => {
      throw new Error("Sentry Test Error");
    });
</script>
```

### [View Captured Data in Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/capacitor.md#view-captured-data-in-sentry)

Now, head over to your project on [Sentry.io](https://sentry.io/) to view the collected data (it takes a couple of moments for the data to appear).

Need help locating captured data in your Sentry project?

* Open the [**Issues**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/issues/) page and select an error from the issues list to view the full details and context of this error. For more details, see the [Issue Details documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-details.md).
* Open the [**Traces**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/traces/) page and select a trace to reveal more information about each span, its duration, and any errors. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-basics/getting-started-tutorial/generate-first-error.md#ui-walkthrough).
* Open the [**Replays**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/replays/) page and select an entry from the list to get a detailed view where you can replay the interaction and get more information to help you troubleshoot.
* Open the [**Logs**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/logs/) page and filter by service, environment, or search keywords to view log entries from your application. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md#overview).
* Open the [**User Feedback**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/feedback/) page and click on individual feedback to see more details all in one view. For more information, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback.md).

# Cloud Functions for Firebase

**URL:** https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md

---
title: "Cloud Functions for Firebase"
description: "Learn how to set up Sentry in your Cloud Functions for Firebase project and capture your first events."
url: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/
---

# Sentry for Cloud Functions for Firebase

[Cloud Functions for Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/docs/functions) let you automatically run backend code in response to events triggered by Firebase features and HTTPS requests. Sentry's Node SDK works out of the box with Cloud Functions for Firebase.

## [What's Instrumented](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#whats-instrumented)

The Sentry SDK includes a built-in [Firebase integration](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/integrations/firebase.md) that automatically instruments:

* **Cloud Functions** - HTTP functions, background functions, and event triggers
* **[Firestore](https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore)** - Database operations like reads, writes, and queries are instrumented out of the box

This integration is enabled by default, so you get automatic performance monitoring and error tracking without any additional configuration.

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#prerequisites)

You need:

* A Sentry [account](https://sentry.io/signup/) and [project](https://docs.sentry.io/product/projects.md)
* Your application up and running
* Node version `20.19.0` or above. Node.js 22 needs `22.12` or higher, while Node.js 23 needs `23.2` or higher (`>=20.19.0 <22.0.0 || >=22.12.0 <23.0.0 || >=23.2.0`).

## [Install](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#install)

### [Install the Sentry SDK](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#install-the-sentry-sdk)

Run the command for your preferred package manager to add the Sentry SDK to your Firebase Functions project:

```bash
npm install @sentry/node @sentry/profiling-node --save
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: yarn, pnpm*

## [Configure](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#configure)

**Error Monitoring** starts working as soon as you call `Sentry.init()`. **Logs** and **Application Metrics** need no extra configuration, and you'll learn how to send them in steps [#3](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#send-logs) and [#4](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#send-application-metrics-). This guide also enables **Tracing** and **Profiling**.

Want to learn more about these features?

* [**Issues**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues.md) (always enabled): Sentry's core error monitoring product that automatically reports errors, uncaught exceptions, and crashes. If you have something that looks like an exception, Sentry can capture it.
* [**Tracing**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/tracing.md): Track software performance while seeing the impact of errors across multiple systems. For example, distributed tracing allows you to follow a request from the frontend to the backend and back.
* [**Profiling**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/profiling.md): Gain deeper insight than traditional tracing without custom instrumentation, letting you discover slow-to-execute or resource-intensive functions in your app.
* [**Logs**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md): Centralize and analyze your application logs to correlate them with errors and performance issues. Search, filter, and visualize log data to understand what's happening in your applications.
* [**Application Metrics**](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md) (always enabled): Track and analyze custom application metrics, such as response times and database query durations, to understand trends and patterns in your application's performance and behavior over time.

Create an initialization file (for example, `instrument.js`) that imports and initializes Sentry.

The snippet also turns on:

* Tracing: via [`tracesSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/options.md#tracesSampleRate)
* Profiling: via [`profileSessionSampleRate`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/options.md#profileSessionSampleRate), [`profileLifecycle`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/options.md#profileLifecycle), and the profiling integration

Don't need a feature? Remove its integration and options from the snippet.

```javascript
const Sentry = require("@sentry/node");
const { nodeProfilingIntegration } = require("@sentry/profiling-node");

Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  integrations: [
    // enables Profiling
    nodeProfilingIntegration(),
  ],

  // Enables Tracing.
  // Set to 1.0 to capture 100% of spans for tracing.
  // We recommend reducing this value in production.
  tracesSampleRate: 1.0,

  // Enables Profiling for every session.
  profileSessionSampleRate: 1.0,
  profileLifecycle: "trace",
});
```

Import the initialization file at the very top of your functions entry point (for example, `index.js`), before any other imports:

It's important that you import the initialization file **before** any other `require` calls, including Firebase imports. This ensures Sentry can properly instrument all modules.

```javascript
require("./instrument"); // Require Sentry initialization first

const { onRequest } = require("firebase-functions/https");
const { onDocumentCreated } = require("firebase-functions/firestore");
const admin = require("firebase-admin");

admin.initializeApp();

// HTTP function - automatically instrumented
exports.helloWorld = onRequest(async (request, response) => {
  response.send("Hello from Firebase!");
});

// Firestore trigger - automatically instrumented
exports.onUserCreated = onDocumentCreated(
  "users/{userId}",
  async (event) => {
    const userId = event.params.userId;
    // Your logic here
  },
);
```

### [Add Readable Stack Traces With Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#add-readable-stack-traces-with-source-maps)

The stack traces in your Sentry errors probably won't look like your actual code without unminifying them. To fix this, upload your source maps to Sentry. The easiest way to do this is by using the Sentry Wizard.

Alternatively, take a look at our [Uploading Source Maps](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/sourcemaps/uploading.md) documentation.

```bash
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i sourcemaps
```

### [Control the Data You Send to Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#control-the-data-you-send-to-sentry)

By default, the SDK sends user identity data (IP address, ID, and similar) and other data like HTTP bodies and URL query parameters. This will give you rich debugging context.

The SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

To send less data, turn off the categories you don't need in the `dataCollection` option. For the full list of categories and their defaults, [see the `dataCollection` options](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/options.md#dataCollection).

```javascript
Sentry.init({
  dsn: "https://<key>@o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/<projectId>",
  dataCollection: {
    userInfo: false,
    // other categories
  },
});
```

## [Send Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#send-logs)

Use `Sentry.logger` to send logs at different levels, such as `info`, `warn`, or `error`. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Logs](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/logs.md) for all available logging methods and the syntax for formatting messages.

```javascript
Sentry.logger.info("User example action completed");

Sentry.logger.warn("Slow operation detected", {
  operation: "data_fetch",
  duration: 3500,
});

Sentry.logger.error("Validation failed", {
  form_field: "email",
  reason: "Invalid email",
});
```

If you're already logging with another library, use an integration to capture those logs as Sentry Logs automatically:

* [`consoleLoggingIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/logs.md#console-integration) for `console` calls
* [Consola](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/logs.md#console-integration)
* [Pino](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/integrations/pino.md)

## [Send Application Metrics NEW](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#send-application-metrics-)

Use `Sentry.metrics` to send counters, gauges, and distributions from your app to Sentry. You can pass any attributes you want and search or filter by them later. See [Set Up Metrics](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/metrics.md) for all available metric types and configuration options.

```javascript
Sentry.metrics.count("checkout.failed", 1);

Sentry.metrics.gauge("time_since_refresh", 4, { unit: "hour" });

Sentry.metrics.distribution("api_latency", 187, {
  unit: "millisecond",
  attributes: { endpoint: "/api/orders" },
});
```

On Node.js, [`nodeRuntimeMetricsIntegration`](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase/configuration/integrations/noderuntimemetrics.md) also collects runtime health metrics automatically.

## [Verify Your Setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#verify-your-setup)

Let's test your setup and confirm that Sentry is working correctly and sending data to your Sentry project.

Add a test function that throws an error, deploy your functions, and trigger the test endpoint:

```javascript
require("./instrument");
const { onRequest } = require("firebase-functions/https");

exports.testSentry = onRequest(async () => {
  throw new Error("Sentry Test Error");
});
```

*Other available variations of the above snippet: bash*

### [View Captured Data in Sentry](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/firebase.md#view-captured-data-in-sentry)

Now, head over to your project on [Sentry.io](https://sentry.io/) to view the collected data (it takes a couple of moments for the data to appear).

Need help locating captured data in your Sentry project?

* Open the [**Issues**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/issues/) page and select an error from the issues list to view the full details and context of this error. For more details, see the [Issue Details documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-details.md).
* Open the [**Traces**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/traces/) page and select a trace to reveal more information about each span, its duration, and any errors. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-basics/getting-started-tutorial/generate-first-error.md#ui-walkthrough).
* Open the [**Profiles**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/profiling/) page to see your slowest functions and an aggregate flame graph of your most frequent code paths. If tracing is enabled, select a transaction to see the flame graph for that part of your app. For more information, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/profiling/profile-details.md).
* Open the [**Logs**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/logs/) page and filter by service, environment, or search keywords to view log entries from your application. For an interactive UI walkthrough, click [here](https://docs.sentry.io/product/logs.md#overview).
* Open the [**Application Metrics**](https://sentry.io/orgredirect/organizations/:orgslug/explore/metrics) page to view and analyze your metrics. For more details, see this [interactive walkthrough](https://docs.sentry.io/product/metrics.md#overview).
